gates.detail: protected columns at rest are ciphertext: every signed-off column was observed and carries the cipher marker, no seeded plaintext survives in the file bytes — and the positive control witnessed the seed in a cipher-disabled control DB. The FILE itself is plain SQLite by design (D22): only the sensitive columns are sealed.

the SEC-AUTH-09 PIN-verifier material (salt, hash, params) is sealed at rest: every user_pin_verifiers column was observed with a non-null value carrying the cipher marker, so the verifier bytes exist on disk only as ciphertext (SEC-AUTH-09 leg 1, on the post-D22 column cipher).

Hermes canonicalizeJcs matches the shared RFC 8785 golden vectors byte-for-byte: 26 number, 1 canonicalization (text + §3.2.4 UTF-8 bytes), and the property-sort (UTF-16 code-unit order) vectors all agree — the on-device hash preimage is identical to the Node engine's (SEC-OPLOG-06).
3 devices converged to the canonical-fold reference under shuffled arrival (3 replicas, 100 ops/device); both §4.2 fold paths fired on every device (502 head-applies, 458 re-folds).
3 devices authored 120 ops offline, reconnected one at a time, and converged to the canonical fold over the wire (3/3 replicas; 686 foreign ops folded, empty redundant pull).

device A delivered 121 ops (all accepted), replayed 61 verbatim (all duplicate), a held-op pull applied 0 with digest + edit_count unchanged, and a novel foreign op still applied (edit_count 100→101) — replay is idempotent (§3.6).

3/3 devices converged on the shared note; the LWW winner "body-207-C-1" is the canonical (timestamp,deviceId,seq) last edit; and edit-after-archive surfaced a significant conflict on device B (note stays archived, the edit stands) — concurrent-edit resolution is correct (§3.6).
